entries.title: II Chronicles 8:3
segments: Hamath-zobah; Zobah was a country north and east of Palestine. Hamath was a city on the river Orontes, apparently belonging to Zobath.

entries.title: II Chronicles 8:4
segments:
Tadmor; a city in the great Syrian desert, between Damascus and the Euphrates.  It was afterwards called Palmyra, and has long been in ruins. 
 
So fading and transitory are all earthly things, the the most splendid cities may become a heap of ruins.  This should lead all to seek a city that hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God.

entries.title: II Chronicles 8:5
segments: Beth-horon the upper, and--the nether; on the border of Ephraim and Benjamin.

entries.title: II Chronicles 8:6
segments: Baalath; a city within the territory of the tribe of Dan.

entries.title: II Chronicles 8:8
segments: Unto this day; see note to

entries.title: II Chronicles 8:11
segments:
The city of David; Zion, the south-western hill of Jerusalem. 
 
  Shall not dwell in the house of David; he seems to have regarded this as too sacred a place for the residence of one who was a foreigner, not of Israelitish descent. 
 
A man's wife has a great influence upon him, and through him upon others; let him be careful that this influence does not mislead him into sinful practice.

entries.title: II Chronicles 8:14
segments: The commands of parents, so far as they accord with the commands of God, should be remembered and carefully followed by their children.

entries.title: II Chronicles 8:17
segments: Ezion-geber, and--Eloth; on the eastern branch of the Red sea.

entries.title: II Chronicles 8:18
segments: Ophir; a distant place visited by ships from the Red sea, the location of which is not known with certainty.  It is generally supposed to have been in either Arabia or India.
